prereq.title: Check Node.js
prereq.note: You need v22 or newer. If it is older, install a current version from nodejs.org and reopen the terminal.

install.title: Install Relay once for the whole machine
install.note: Then type starci-relay --version. A version number means it worked; from now on you only type starci-relay.

login.title: Connect the machine to your account
login.note: Relay prints an 8-character code. Press Connect a machine, enter the code, check the machine name and confirm. Check with starci-relay status.

service.title: Start Relay at login (optional)
service.note: Only needed when you want your AI to run scenarios on this machine without a terminal open. It runs at user level, with no admin right. Relay runs StarCi-signed requests without asking each time, so turn it on only on your own machine. Turn it off with starci-relay uninstall-service.

update.title: Update
update.note: Run the install command again with @latest, then type starci-relay --version to see the new version.

remove.title: Remove
remove.note: Turn off the auto-start first, then remove the package. To drop the machine from your account, revoke it in the paired machines list.

notFound.title: starci-relay: command not found
notFound.note: The terminal does not see npm's global folder yet. Open a new terminal after installing. If it still fails, run npm config get prefix and add that folder (Windows) or its bin folder (macOS, Linux) to PATH.

node.title: Wrong Node version
node.note: Relay needs Node 22 or newer. Run node --version to see what you have.

permission.title: EACCES while installing on macOS or Linux
permission.note: Do not use sudo. Point npm's prefix at a folder in your home (npm config set prefix ~/.npm-global) and add ~/.npm-global/bin to PATH.

code.title: The code is wrong or has expired
code.note: A code lives a few minutes. Run starci-relay login again for a new one.

service.title: install-service says it could not start right away
service.note: The auto-start file is written anyway; log in again and Relay runs. Type starci-relay status to see whether it is on.

connectAi.canText: Read the unlocked parts of a lesson, read and search the source at the lesson's pinned commit, see the scenarios, your own run results and the laws you have opened. Ask your machine to re-run one scenario: the command shows on your machine and runs only when you confirm. Source, scenarios and re-runs need Premium like the lesson workspace.

lead.setup: The code runs on your machine and never leaves it. The relay is a small program that links your machine to this page: it downloads the lesson, starts the services in Docker, runs each case and reports back here.

intro.outcomeAnswer: Answer the interview question above in full, with code you have run
intro.diagramLabel: Diagram of the lab's services: the customer calls the entry service, which calls the others, and each service has its own database
intro.diagramError: The diagram could not be drawn
intro.diagramCaption: A solid arrow is a call between services. A dashed line joins a service to its own database and to what it uses. The service that shows a file name holds the file you edit.

loop.lockedNote: Opens when the question before it passes.
loop.runTitle: Run this case on your machine
loop.runNote: Type the command in the lesson folder. The relay runs this case and every case before it, then reports back to this page.
loop.diffNote: Open because this case passed. The command prints where your file differs from the reference.
loop.resetNote: Stuck for good? Bring this case's reference step to your machine.
loop.resetWarning: Your file is not lost: the relay keeps it on the branch cua-toi-luu-{caseId} before it changes anything.
loop.mcpTitle: Ask an AI teaching assistant in your own tools
loop.mcpNote: Run the command below in the lesson folder. Your AI (Claude, ChatGPT) can read the real runs, open hints and ask your machine to run again. How to connect is on the Connect AI page.
loop.happyIntro: There is nothing to fix yet. Run these cases to see the current code do the right thing when nothing goes wrong. Remember what right looks like: on the next page you will spot the difference at once.
loop.unhappyIntro: Each case is a follow-up an interviewer would throw at you. Run it, see what is not right yet, edit your file and run it again until it passes. The next question opens when the one before it passes.
